summary: Gone 1930 frame cabin lookout on McClure Mountain near Twisp; the summit now has communication towers and a road across private land.

facts.design: frame cabin; no plan or size given in sources

access.note: Hikers reach the summit on foot over National Forest land. The summit road crosses private land and is not open to the public. A seasonal forest road gate may be closed

visit.trail_note: Motorcycle trail from forest road FR 225, reached from Twisp via Lookout Mountain Road; TrailChick describes a ridge route from Lookout Mountain Road

events.note: Frame cabin built in 1930 according to Ray Kresek as relayed by WillhiteWeb; the register and FireLookout.com agree
Panorama photographs of the lookout dated August 8, 1934, credited to the National Archives Pacific Northwest Region
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register November 17, 2012

evidence.supports: frame cabin built in 1930 and now gone
evidence.quote: Built in 1930, this frame cabin is now gone.
Kresek reports a frame cabin built in 1930.

evidence.supports: no maps or images of the lookout are known
evidence.quote: That is all we got, no maps or images showing the lookout.

evidence.supports: TrailChick says a lookout cabin stood there in the 1930s, with little known about it
evidence.quote: little information is known about the site
McClure was home to a fire lookout cabin sometime in the 1930s

evidence.supports: panorama photographs of the lookout dated 1934 from the National Archives
evidence.quote: McClure Mountain Lookout panoramic 8-8-1934 (N) - courtesy of National Archives-Pacific Northwest Region

evidence.supports: numerous communication towers on the summit and difficulty placing the cabin
evidence.quote: Today there are numerous communication towers on top and evidence of many previous towers so it is difficult to pinpoint which spot the cabin could have been located.

evidence.supports: best guess for the cabin site is a rocky knob at the far east point
evidence.quote: The highest and most likely is a rocky knob at the far east point.

evidence.supports: summit road crosses private land and is not open to the public
evidence.quote: it crosses through private land and isn't open for public use

evidence.supports: road used for communication and radio equipment on the summit
evidence.quote: The road is used primarily for the maintenance of communication and radio equipment on the summit.

evidence.supports: ridge route on National Forest land
evidence.quote: a route completely on National Forest land

evidence.supports: motorcycle trail goes the whole way to the summit
evidence.quote: A nice motorcycle trail goes the whole way.

evidence.supports: seasonal gate usually open by May, not known for sure
evidence.quote: The gate is usually open by May but I do not know for sure.

evidence.supports: McClure is a prominent high point near Twisp
evidence.quote: a prominent high point here in Twisp near my home

notes_for_editor: Two of the four sources are web guides that repeat the 1930 date from Kresek's book, which was not reached, so the date rests on one secondhand citation. No staffing, fire or removal date found. The register and FireLookout.com say gone; TrailChick gives only the decade. The exact cabin site is unknown, and WillhiteWeb's rocky-knob guess is not confirmed. The access note combines WillhiteWeb's route and TrailChick's ridge route.
